items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar date for payment: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026'. A printed calendar date is used as written (no period-counting needed). 06.08.2026 is a Thursday, not a weekend or public holiday in NW, so no shift under §193 BGB is relevant here.

warnings: This letter shows multiple hallmarks of a fake/scam debt collection ('Fake-Inkasso') letter: it demands payment to a foreign personal IBAN (Lithuania, account holder A. Petrauskas) rather than a business account in Germany, which is highly unusual and risky for a supposed German debt collector.

The extremely short 72-hour deadline combined with threats of account seizure (Kontopfändung), a negative SCHUFA entry, and criminal prosecution for 'Eingehungsbetrug' without any mention of a court judgment or enforceable title (Vollstreckungstitel) is a classic high-pressure scam tactic; a genuine Kontopfändung legally requires a prior court title, which this letter does not reference.

The letter falsely claims that objecting ('Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos') is pointless and will only cause further costs — this is misleading; recipients always retain the right to dispute a claim, and this statement should be treated as manipulative pressure rather than legal fact.

'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' phone-contract claims from Cyprus-registered collection agencies are a well-known German consumer-protection scam pattern; the person should verify whether such a phone contract was ever actually concluded before considering any payment, and should not pay funds to the IBAN given without independent verification.

No original creditor contract details, dates of the alleged phone agreement, or proof of the claim are provided — only a lump-sum figure with added collection fees, which is inconsistent with standard German debt-collection documentation requirements.
